The evidence suggests that L-cystine binds to Ctns, which is involved in sulfur amino acid transport, and this interaction leads to the participation of Ctns in the transport activity, ultimately resulting in Slc7a11 being a participant in this process. Similarly, L-cystine binds to Slc3a1, which also participates in sulfur amino acid transport, and this pathway also leads to Slc7a11 being a participant. These findings highlight a shared mechanism where L-cystine influences the activity of transporters involved in sulfur amino acid transport, which in turn affects Slc7a11. The integration of these pathways underscores a potential role for L-cystine in modulating the function of Slc7a11 through its interaction with transport-related proteins. The evidence supports a direct link between L-cystine and Slc7a11 via a pathway involving sulfur amino acid transporters, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
